clue.text: Monarchy suffering endlessly upsetting drama

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the whole construction upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: the United Kingdom is a monarchy, abbreviated UK

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: agony is great suffering

explanation.surface: A grumble that a monarchy which suffers without end makes for distressing drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims AGONY to AGON; 'upsetting' turns UK + AGON upside down. 'drama' looks like part of the moan but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nogaku is the formal name for classical Japanese Noh theatre, a form of stage drama.

clue.text: Stop castaway cutting braces

indicators.note: a brace is a pair, so cutting braces removes a pair of letters from the front of each half of the clue word, cast and away

explanation.surface: A stranded sailor is told to halt as he hacks at the struts of his shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read castaway as CAST + AWAY; 'cutting braces' removes a brace (two letters) from the head of each, CA and AW, leaving ST + AY.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or halt where you are, a straightforward synonym for stopping.

clue.text: Jewish guy praised for working outside hospital

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go around the hospital letter
for working says the letters of praised are put to work in a new order

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A man of the Jewish faith is commended for his work at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for working' rearranges PRAISED to SEPARDI, and 'outside' wraps that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Sephardim are Jews descended from the communities of Spain and Portugal, so one such man fits.

clue.text: Old sailor in the hold

definitions.meaning: Admiral Horatio ..., the Royal Navy's hero of Trafalgar
a wrestling grip applied from behind under the arms

explanation.surface: An elderly seaman down in a ship's cargo space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hold' suggests a ship's hold to suit the sailor; it is the wrestling hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral of Trafalgar fame and the wrestling grip share one surname-turned-noun.

clue.text: Who could slam disheartened robber with judge on guard?

definitions.text: Who could slam disheartened robber with judge on guard?

indicators.note: slam suggests violent bashing, so the gathered letters are knocked into a new order
disheartened says the middle letters of robber are removed, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A question about who could condemn a thief while a judge keeps watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves RR from ROBBER; 'slam' rearranges RR + J + ON + GUARD. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a jury that decides whether to indict could send a robber to trial, a slam in the critical sense.

clue.text: Church blocking question on dodgy issue goes shtum

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the question letter comes first
blocking says the church letters sit inside, obstructing the jumbled letters
dodgy means unreliable, signalling the letters of issue are jumbled

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church that refuses to answer a question on a dubious matter keeps its mouth shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes shtum' is the definition, slang for falling silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiesce is to become quiet or still, and going shtum is slang for falling silent.

clue.text: Suppress courage completely

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
up means completely, as in eat up or use up

explanation.surface: An instruction to stifle bravery entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTLE for courage is British slang, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle up feelings is to keep them in, the same as suppressing them.

clue.text: Unruly pupil manages to hide unknown rags

indicators.note: to hide says the unknown letter is tucked inside the jumbled letters
unruly says the letters of the pupil phrase are out of order

parts.note: Z is an algebraic unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A badly behaved schoolchild manages to conceal some old clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unruly' rearranges PUPIL MANAGES, and 'to hide' puts Z inside. 'rags' looks like cloth but means cheap papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive word for a low-grade publication; the sensational fiction periodicals on cheap paper are exactly that.

clue.text: Reprimand received by 23 12

indicators.note: received by says the answer is held within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answers to 23 across and 12 across, written one after the other

explanation.surface: A telling-off taken in by two cross-referenced entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 23 and 12 side by side; the answer straddles the join. 9, 12, 19 and 23 are all found inside one another this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting an earful means receiving a long scolding, so it serves as a noun for a telling-off.

clue.text: Possibly gooey kiss planted in style

indicators.note: planted in says the kiss letter is set inside the style word

parts.note: way means manner or style
X is the cross used for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A sloppy kiss slipped in stylishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something waxy is soft and sticky like wax, and so may be described as gooey.

clue.text: Guardian magazine almost switched round small part of chapter?

indicators.note: switched round says the guardian part and the magazine part trade places
almost says the last letter of the magazine name is dropped

parts.note: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an angel, as in guardian angel, watches over someone

explanation.surface: A newspaper's magazine nearly reshuffled around a small bit of a chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian magazine' looks like the newspaper's weekend supplement; the words split apart. Hello! is a British celebrity magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The motorcycle club is organised into local chapters, so a member is a part of one; the question mark flags the non-book sense.

clue.text: Bird trapped in 9 19

indicators.note: trapped in says the answer is caught inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answers to 9 across and 19 across, written one after the other

explanation.surface: A bird caught in two cross-referenced entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 9 and 19 side by side; the bird straddles the join.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey-and-white seabird of the petrel family found on northern cliffs.

clue.text: Gauge foreign capital in new metric

indicators.note: in says the capital goes inside the rearranged letters
new says the letters of metric are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, foreign from a British view

explanation.surface: Measuring a foreign capital city with a new metric system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges METRIC to MICTER, and ROME goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A micrometer is a precision measuring instrument, and a gauge is any measuring device.

clue.text: Climbs, dropping over/around short squat deer

indicators.note: around says the climbing word goes round the shortened squat word
dropping says the over letter is let fall from the climbing word

parts.note: mounts means climbs, as one mounts stairs
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: short says the last letter of the squat word is removed

parts.note: jack, as in jack squat, is slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: Deer described as climbing about while losing height, short and stocky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squat' looks like stocky, but it is the slang phrase 'jack squat', meaning nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Muntjacs are small Asian deer, also naturalised in Britain, known for their barking call.

clue.text: Reordering drinks for those providing fundamental sports coverage

parts.note: cycling letters is a way of reordering them, moving them round in a loop
shorts are small measures of spirits

explanation.surface: Rearranging the drinks for the people who supply basic sports coverage, like broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reordering' looks like an anagram signal but is simply CYCLING; 'fundamental' puns on the fundament, the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight Lycra garments worn on the bike cover the fundament, the backside, during sport.

clue.text: Separated husband and wife stopping to receive food

indicators.note: separated says the two spouses are not put in together but at different places
stopping says the spouse letters plug gaps inside the receiving phrase

parts.note: come in is what a host says to receive a visitor

explanation.surface: A separated couple pause to collect a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separated' and 'stopping' put H and W apart inside COME IN: C-H-O-W-MEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow mein is a Chinese dish of stir-fried noodles, a familiar takeaway meal.

clue.text: Literally divided insecure country of birth

indicators.note: literally divided says to split the next word letter for letter at a natural break, into in plus secure, and read each part separately

parts.note: split into in and secure: being in is being at home, and to secure a contract is to land it

explanation.surface: Feeling torn and unsafe about one's native land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally divided' tells you to split 'insecure' into IN + SECURE and treat each half as a clue word: in = HOME (at home), secure = LAND (to land a deal).
explanation.definitionFit: One's native land, where one was born, is the usual sense of this word.

clue.text: Chord discovered, ingenuity having fed Australian pianist

indicators.note: discovered says the covering outer letters of chord are removed
having fed says the ingenuity word is put inside the Australian word

parts.note: Oz is informal for Australia
wit means cleverness or ingenuity

explanation.surface: A musical chord revealed, cleverness feeding an Australian keyboard player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian pianist' tempts as one phrase, but the pianist was Russian-born and Australian gives only the slang for the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Horowitz was a celebrated twentieth-century concert pianist.

clue.text: Little picture capturing bottom of Friar Tuck?

indicators.note: capturing says the small picture word holds the other letter inside

parts.note: an inset is a small picture set within a larger one

indicators.note: bottom of a down clue word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A small image showing Friar Tuck's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friar Tuck' looks like Robin Hood's monk; 'bottom of Friar' gives R and Tuck is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To tuck something in is to put it in, a verb sense of insert; the question mark flags the hidden verb.

clue.text: Swimmer submerged in 12 23 …

indicators.note: submerged in says the answer lies beneath the surface of the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answers to 12 across and 23 across, written one after the other

explanation.surface: A swimmer under the water in two cross-referenced entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 12 and 23 side by side; the fish straddles the join. The ellipsis carries this answer into 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A marlin is a large fast ocean fish with a spear-like snout, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Digital icon partly used in style

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A computer icon that is partly used in fashionable design.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles DigITAL ICon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type is one of the font styles a typesetter picks, so it is used in style.

clue.text: … upset with Poe's objective?

indicators.note: upset says the combined letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the ellipsis carries over the answer to the previous clue, 19 across

explanation.surface: Read on from 19, a fish upset by Poe's work; is it objective?
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis brings in MARLIN from 19 across; 'upset' rearranges MARLIN + POES.
explanation.definitionFit: Objective means detached and free of personal feeling, which is close to a synonym; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Jimi's third guitar returned for test

indicators.note: returned says the pieces are read back to front
third picks out the third letter of the name

parts.note: axe is musicians' slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: Jimi Hendrix's third guitar is sent back for a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third' gives M from JIMI'S; 'returned' turns M + AXE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is an examination, a formal test of knowledge.

clue.text: Flat numbers 7 and 11 have this in common

definitions.meaning: flat means level, as a smooth surface is

definitions.text: numbers 7 and 11 have this in common
definitions.meaning: the number words seven and eleven both end in the same four letters

explanation.walkthrough: '7 and 11' look like grid references but are the numbers spelt out: sEVEN and elEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level or smooth, as flat ground is; the other half is a cryptic hint.

clue.text: One-dimensional component of 19 9

indicators.note: component of says the answer is a part within the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answers to 19 across and 9 across, written one after the other

explanation.surface: A one-dimensional part of two cross-referenced entries.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 19 and 9 side by side; the answer straddles the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extending along a single line has only length, which is to say it has one dimension.

clue.text: In fairness, unusual type

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of fairness come in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: In the interests of fairness, an unusual sort of person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges FAIRNESS. 'type' looks like a kind of person; it is printing type.
explanation.definitionFit: Typefaces without the small finishing strokes on letters form a family of printing type.
